**English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) > **中文文档入口：[文档目录](docs/README.zh-CN.md) · [安装与启动](docs/getting-started.md) · [开发指南](docs/development.md)**
# SoduWork ## The AI-native engine for teams and their agents **A chat ends with an answer. A SoduWork request ends when the person who asked signs off.** **Multi-harness · Multi-agent · Self-hosted** Works with Pi · OpenCode · DeepSeek Harness · Qwen Code · Kimi Code · Codex Harness · Codex ```sh git clone https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork cd SoduWork ``` | Platform | Start command | | --- | --- | | macOS / Linux | `sh start.sh --desktop` | | Windows PowerShell | `.\start.cmd --desktop` | | Windows Command Prompt | `start.cmd --desktop` | [Website](https://soduwork.ai) | [Live demo](https://soduwork.ai) | [Documentation](docs/README.md) | [Docs website](https://dev.soduwork.ai) | [Releases](https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork/releases) | [Discord](https://discord.gg/AXYNrAYHy) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/mdiri-ai/SoduWork)](https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork/releases) [![Platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20macOS%20%7C%20Linux-lightgrey.svg)](#quick-start) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/chat-Discord-5865F2.svg)](https://discord.gg/AXYNrAYHy)
--- ## What SoduWork can do for you | | | | --- | --- | | **One harness does the work, another reviews it** | Pick Pi to do the work. OpenCode, on a different model, reviews it against the acceptance criteria. If the review fails, the work goes back with the reasons. | | **Hand a request to a colleague's agent** | People and AI work together: you file a request, AI writes the acceptance criteria, and you assign it to yourself or a colleague. The assignee's agent does the work and reviews it, and a person signs off. Everyone on the request can see who did what. | | **Turn one person's know-how into a team asset** | When you and AI get a task right, save the chat as a plugin. After review, anyone on the team can use it and contribute improvements, with access granted as needed. | ## Core ideas
**🔀 Smart dispatch** **The right agent and model for each job.** - Pick a harness for each step and switch mid-conversation - Routine steps on cheap or local models, strong models where it matters - Long tasks go to your own cloud runner **🛡️ Built-in governance** **Your organization decides which AI does what, and where.** - Plugins are reviewed before they are shared, granted to teams or people, and can be revoked - Roles, usage, cost and an audit log - Self-hosted **✅ Verified delivery** **Set the bar first. Done means the requester signed off.** - Every request carries its acceptance criteria - A separate AI review checks each one - A person makes the final call
## Quick start > SoduWork is in public beta. Try it and tell us what you think, and evaluate it before using it in production. You need Python 3.12+, Node.js 22.19+ and Git. From the cloned repository, run `sh start.sh --desktop` on macOS/Linux, `.\start.cmd --desktop` in Windows PowerShell, or `start.cmd --desktop` in Command Prompt. The first run installs dependencies, then starts the Hub, the admin console and the desktop client on this computer. Set a password for the `admin` account (12–128 characters) when asked. Then add a model provider under **Model catalog** in the admin console, start a chat in the client and try a small task. Pi is built in. ### Already added an API key? Start here 1. **Add a chat model as well.** Under **Capabilities → Model catalog**, find the service you connected, choose **Add model**, enter the provider's exact model ID, select **Chat model**, and save. Saving a service credential alone does not create a selectable model. 2. **Open the desktop client and sign in to the same Hub.** Use `--desktop` when starting from source. The browser admin console configures the service; check that **Connection** on the desktop sign-in screen points to that same Hub. 3. **Choose New conversation, Pi, and the model you added.** Pi uses the SoduWork model catalog. Codex uses its own account and needs its own sign-in; it does not automatically use this API key. 4. **Try a small task.** For example: “Turn these fictional meeting notes into an action table with owner and due date. Mark missing information as unconfirmed: Alex will organize the requirements by Friday; Sam will check the quotation.” Check the returned table against the notes. 5. **Create a requirement when you need assignment and acceptance.** Describe the goal, inputs and acceptance criteria, open **Arrange execution**, choose an Agent and model, and inspect the delivery before accepting it. A normal conversation does not require a project, plugin or automation first. For the first message, use an **OpenAI-compatible chat model with Pi**. A successful connection probe does not guarantee a successful inference: balance, model permissions and protocol support still matter. If the Agent list is empty, check **Agent management** and the Runner connection. If the model list is empty, check that the model exists, is enabled, and both interfaces use the same Hub. See [Run from source: send your first AI message](docs/getting-started.en.md#send-your-first-ai-message) for field-by-field setup and troubleshooting.
Try the live demo Download the client from [Releases](https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork/releases/latest), enter `https://service.soduwork.ai` under **Connection** on the sign-in screen, then sign up and sign in. > The demo is for evaluation only. Don't upload real business data or anything sensitive.
Install the desktop client Follow the illustrated [desktop installation and first conversation guide](docs/desktop-quickstart.en.md). | OS | Package | | --- | --- | | Windows | `SoduWork--Setup.exe` | | macOS (Apple Silicon / Intel) | `SoduWork--mac-.dmg` | | Linux | `SoduWork--linux.deb` / `.rpm` / `.tar.gz` | Download from [Releases](https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork/releases). On first launch, enter your Hub address under **Connection**, then sign in. On macOS, if you see "cannot verify the developer", open **System Settings → Privacy & Security** and choose **Open Anyway**.
Deploy for a team with Docker With Docker installed and running, from the repository root: ```bash python3 ops/self-host/deploy.py up python3 ops/self-host/deploy.py credentials # show the initial admin password ``` This starts the Hub, the admin console and PostgreSQL on one server. Put an HTTPS reverse proxy in front of it to open it to your team. See [Deploy with Docker](https://dev.soduwork.ai/docs/get-started/docker) and [Deploy for a team](https://dev.soduwork.ai/docs/deploy).
Ports, data folders and troubleshooting are in [Run from source](https://dev.soduwork.ai/docs/get-started/run-from-source) and the [FAQ](https://dev.soduwork.ai/docs/get-started/faq). ## Why SoduWork AI agents give everyone fast output. What no one gets for free is trust in that output — or a way to keep what worked. That's where individuals and teams get stuck alike: | The problem | What SoduWork does | | --- | --- | | **Fast output, slow trust** — whether you work alone or in a team, the time AI saves goes back into checking what it produced | **The request is the spec.** Criteria set before work starts; a separate AI review checks each one; a person signs off | | **What worked dies in a chat thread** — for one person, it's last month's perfect run you can't reproduce; for a team, it's one person's method nobody else can use | **Get it right once, keep it as a plugin.** Reuse it yourself or publish it for everyone — every improvement reaches everyone | | **A drawer full of AI tools** — three subscriptions and no standard for which one does what | **One workbench, your playbook.** Your plugins run on every harness. Switch mid-conversation, keep your history and files | | **Results that never enter the workflow** — output gets copy-pasted around, and every handoff re-explains the background | **Issues that carry the context.** People and agents pick up where it left off, with a full record of who did what | ## How it works Requests, execution, review and reuse all happen in one shared issue pool: ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Raise a request] --> B[AI refines it
adds acceptance criteria] B --> C[Assign
yourself · a colleague · an agent] C --> D[Agent runs it
with a team plugin] D --> E[AI review
assignee confirms] E --> F[Requester signs off] F --> G[Save as a plugin] G -.reused by the team.-> D ``` | Role | Where they join | | --- | --- | | **Solo developer** | Puts requests in the pool, lets agents work through them, and only signs off | | **Specialist** | Gets a task right with AI, saves the method as a plugin, and publishes it to the team | | **Manager** | Drops in a request; AI fills in the criteria and routes it to a person or an agent; signs off at the end | | **New team member** | Uses the plugins the organization has built up to do the work to team standards, and improves them when they find a gap | Who asked, who did the work, which plugin ran and who approved it is always on record. ## Multi-harness · Multi-agent A harness is the agent runtime that does the work. It is not the model. SoduWork connects every harness through one adapter interface, so issues, plugins and review don't depend on any single harness. Switch harnesses mid-conversation and keep the history and the working folder. Programs that support the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) can be added with a catalog declaration.
Supported harnesses (9) | Harness | Models | How it connects | | --- | --- | --- | | Pi | Your SoduWork models | Built in | | OpenCode | Your SoduWork models | Native adapter, installed on demand | | DeepSeek Harness | Your SoduWork models, or your own DeepSeek key | ACP, installed on demand | | Qwen Code | Your SoduWork models | ACP, installed on demand | | Kimi Code | Your SoduWork models | ACP, installed on demand | | Codex Harness | Your SoduWork models | ACP, installed on demand | | Codex | Its own OpenAI account | Native adapter, installed on demand |
Agents work together at several levels: | Level | Who decides | Example | | --- | --- | --- | | Harness | The harness itself | OpenCode or Qwen Code starts its own subagents to explore the code or split a task | | Single method | A Skill or plugin sets the method, process, rules and what counts as done | A review plugin tells the agent which checks to run and what evidence to attach | | Combined methods | A plugin workflow picks the harness, Skill and model for each step | Pi drafts, Qwen Code checks the sources, and the run stops if the check fails | | People and agents | The requester and the assignee or their agent | A request goes to a colleague, their agent does the work, the requester signs off | | In parallel | The Hub | Different issues run on different agents at the same time, including on cloud runners | Between steps and between people, work moves the way the plugin and the assignee say. Agents don't hand work to other agents on their own. ## Plugins and apps A skill tells AI how to do something. An agent wraps AI into an assistant. SoduWork plugins and apps turn the way your team works into something that **runs, gets verified, improves and stays governed**. | | Skill | Agent | SoduWork plugin | SoduWork app | | --- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | **What it is** | A method doc that AI reads and follows | Prompts, knowledge, tools or a platform flow | A versioned package: method, inputs, acceptance criteria, workflow | A plugin with its own UI
and an AI chat panel | | **Best for** | A single technique | One type of task | Standard team work, run by AI | Repeated work in a dedicated UI | | **How you use it** | AI picks it up | Inside its platform | `/` in chat · on issues · in automations | Its own window + AI sidebar | | **Step-by-step process** | ✗ | ◐ | ✓ | ✓ | | **Choose and switch harness** | ✗ | ◐ | ✓ | ✓ | | **Criteria, AI review, sign-off** | ✗ | ◐ | ✓ | ✓ | | **Versioning** | ✗ | ◐ | ✓ | ✓ | | **UI and interaction** | ✗ | ◐ Chat | ◐ Chat | ✓ | | **Review, grant, revoke** | ◐ Configurable | ◐ Configurable | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ Supported　◐ Partial　✗ Not supported. "Agent" means an assistant built on a typical agent platform; capabilities vary by platform. **From your chat to your playbook — yours or the team's**: create or save a plugin in chat → pre-check and try it locally → keep it for yourself, or submit it for review and publish it to the team catalog. Solo use stays light; team sharing adds review, grants and versioning.
Example: a weekly brief checked against its sources ```json { "schemaVersion": 1, "key": "weekly-brief", "version": "1.0.0", "name": "Weekly brief", "workflow": { "nodes": [ { "key": "draft", "type": "ai", "config": { "agentKind": "local:pi", "prompt": "Write deliverables/brief.md from this week's tasks." } }, { "key": "check", "type": "ai_review", "dependsOn": ["draft"], "config": { "agentKind": "local:qwen", "prompt": "Check each claim against the sources. Block if any claim has no source." } }, { "key": "done", "type": "publish", "dependsOn": ["check"] } ] } } ```
You don't have to write this by hand: describe the work to Plugin Developer in a chat and it produces the file. See the [plugin guide](https://dev.soduwork.ai/docs/plugins) and [apps](https://dev.soduwork.ai/docs/apps). ## How SoduWork compares - **vs. low-code agent builders**: no canvas, no wiring nodes. Finish a real task and save it as a plugin. Agents work directly on real files and projects, locally or in the cloud. - **vs. coding agent harnesses**: SoduWork doesn't replace them. It runs them as harnesses inside a team workspace and adds what they don't have: issues that flow from request to execution to sign-off, independent AI review, plugin review and distribution, and access control with audit. - **vs. multi-agent orchestrators**: people set the steps and checkpoints, and the requester accepts the delivery on evidence. Work moves between steps and people the way the plugin and the assignee say. - **vs. AI office assistants**: know-how doesn't stay in one person's chat history. It becomes a reviewed, versioned plugin — reused by future you tomorrow, and by the whole team next month.
Comparison table | | Low-code agent builders | Coding agent harnesses | Multi-agent orchestrators | AI office assistants | SoduWork | | --- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | Domain experts build and refine agents in chat | ◐ | — | — | ◐ | ✓ | | Engineering and non-engineering work | ✓ | ◐ | ◐ | ✓ | ✓ | | Mix harnesses and models as needed | ◐ | — | ✓ | — | ✓ | | Acceptance criteria built into requests, sign-off on evidence | — | — | ◐ | — | ✓ | | Plugin review, publishing and scoped access | ◐ | — | — | ◐ | ✓ | | Enterprise-grade production and team collaboration | ◐ | ✓ | ◐ | ◐ | ✓ | | Ready to use without building a business layer | — | ✓ | — | ✓ | ✓ | | Hosted service | ✓ | ◐ | ◐ | ✓ | ◐ Self-hosted | ✓ Supported　◐ Partial or varies by product　— Not supported. Based on how each category typically works.
## Architecture **The hard parts, handled:** | Hard part | How SoduWork handles it | | --- | --- | | Clients disagreeing about facts | The Hub is the single source of truth: issues, workflows, approvals and evidence live in the Hub, so every client sees the same facts | | Agents getting access they shouldn't have | Access is granted, not assumed: organization policy, runtime availability and the user's choices together decide what a session can use. Installing something doesn't authorize it | | Lock-in to one harness | One adapter interface for every harness: higher layers never depend on a particular harness. Switch harnesses mid-conversation and keep the history and working folder | | Methods that can't move | Method and environment are separate: plugins define the method; harness, model, runner and secrets are chosen when the plugin is bound. Plugin versions are immutable and portable | | Work nobody can trace | Interaction and execution are separate: the client handles chat and approvals; the runtime and runners do the work — locally or remotely — and every run lands in the audit record |

Inside the runner

The runner connects to the Hub over a WebSocket. Every dispatch has an ID, so the same task is never taken twice. Each harness runs in its own subprocess. Events are saved on the execution host before they are sent, and are sent again after a disconnect.
Known limits - **Cloud handoff moves context, not processes**: the working files, conversation and goal move to the cloud runner. Running processes and browser sessions don't, and you bring your own server. - **A plugin isn't always a workflow**: a plugin can just provide a method or a tool. Workflows are for multi-step work, approval points and resuming after failures. - **Runners and skills are not a general-purpose sandbox**: actual isolation depends on the harness and your environment. Only connect runners to a Hub you trust.
## Where does my data go? - When you self-host, issues, plugins and chat history are stored in your own Hub, and tasks run in the folder you choose. - Model requests go from the runner to the model provider you configure. Each run gets a short-lived credential; keys are not written to the harness's config files in plain text. - Prompts and files sent to a model provider or connector you configure are visible to that service. With self-hosted models, inference can stay in your environment. **Telemetry and updates.** This public source does not include a separate analytics or crash-reporting upload to MDiRi. The client defaults to `https://service.soduwork.ai`; its operational requests go to the Hub selected under **Connection** on the sign-in screen. You can change this address, and your saved selection is kept across restarts and upgrades. Using the hosted service sends those requests to its operator. Selecting your own Hub keeps this traffic with your deployment. - The selected Hub receives device/account authentication and the data required by the features you use. Usage accounting includes the conversation ID and title, Agent/model/provider identifiers, token and cost counters, and timestamps. Update attempts report version, progress, status and errors. These are operational records, not an optional analytics subscription. - Installed clients check the selected Hub for updates at startup and periodically (every six hours). Checks include the current version, platform, CPU architecture and update channel, authenticated with the device session. Source-launched clients skip installer update checks. There is currently no separate setting to disable Hub accounting or installed-client update polling; use your own Hub to avoid sending this traffic to the hosted service. Release-note requests also use the selected Hub. - Hub request/database performance statistics are maintained within the Hub process; they are not automatically exported to MDiRi. Dependencies and optional Agent downloads contact their configured package registries or mirrors, and models/connectors contact the services you configure. Those services have their own data policies. ## FAQ
I work alone. Is SoduWork overkill for me? Not if any of these hold: you re-check AI output yourself, you can't reproduce last month's perfect workflow, or you just want your AI tools to share one standard. Solo use needs no team setup — run it locally with SQLite in one command, and the organization features simply stay unused until you need them. Same plugins, same workbench, more people when you want them.
Is this just another agent platform or orchestrator? SoduWork doesn't replace agent harnesses — it runs them inside a team workspace and adds the layer they don't have: one shared issue pool from request to sign-off, acceptance criteria built into every issue, an independent AI review step, plugin review with scoped grants, and an audit trail. People set the steps, checkpoints and approvals.
Is this actively maintained, or is it a demo? It's an active public beta. Every release has release notes, and the release pipeline runs repository checks and test suites before a version is published. See the [Roadmap](#roadmap) for what's next, and [Contributing](#contributing) if you want to join.
Why do I need to sign in, and where is my data? Accounts underpin organizations, permissions, collaboration and audit. When you self-host, you sign in to your own Hub and your data is stored there. See [Where does my data go?](#where-does-my-data-go)
More answers are in the [FAQ on the developer site](https://dev.soduwork.ai/docs/get-started/faq). ## Roadmap | Status | Item | | --- | --- | | ✅ Shipped | Cloud runner (Personal Agent) support | | In progress | Development kits for plugins and apps | | In progress | Sandbox management for cloud runners | | In progress | Web and mobile apps | | Planned | Marketplace support for apps and plugins in enterprise and private deployments | Ideas are welcome in [Discussions](https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork/discussions). ## Community - **Chat**: [Discord](https://discord.gg/AXYNrAYHy) - **Bugs and feature requests**: [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork/issues) - **Questions and ideas**: [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork/discussions) - **Enterprise**: private deployment, integration and support. Email [contact@soduwork.ai](mailto:contact@soduwork.ai). ## Contributing Issues, ideas, plugins, docs and code are all welcome. 1. Read the [contributing guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) for local setup and the checks to run before a pull request. 2. Fork, create a branch and commit your changes. 3. Open a pull request with a description of the change and how you tested it.
Developer guides | Goal | Read | | --- | --- | | Build a plugin | [Plugin guide](https://dev.soduwork.ai/docs/plugins) | | Build an app | [Apps](https://dev.soduwork.ai/docs/apps) | | Add a harness | [Add an ACP harness](https://dev.soduwork.ai/docs/harnesses/add-acp-harness) | | Deploy and operate | [Deploy for a team](https://dev.soduwork.ai/docs/deploy) | | Commands and configuration | [Reference](https://dev.soduwork.ai/docs/reference/commands) |
### Contributors ## Security Please don't report security issues in public issues. Follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) to report them privately. ## License and acknowledgements SoduWork's own code is copyright MDiRi and released under the [MIT License](LICENSE). Third-party code, fonts, graphics and bundled tools keep their own licenses; see [Third-party notices](https://dev.soduwork.ai/docs/reference/third-party). The SoduWork name and logo are trademarks of MDiRi and are not licensed under MIT. Thanks to Electron, React, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy and the wider open-source ecosystem, and to the agent projects SoduWork runs. Being listed here doesn't mean a project endorses SoduWork.

# SoduWork ## 企业级 AI 原生引擎 **数字 AI 员工，先有数字方法论：沉淀团队最佳实践，驱动多岗位、多 Agent 接力与协同。** **多底座 · 多 Agent · 私有化部署** 支持 Pi · OpenCode · DeepSeek Harness · Qwen Code · Kimi Code · Codex Harness · Codex ```sh git clone https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork cd SoduWork ``` | 系统 | 启动命令 | | --- | --- | | macOS / Linux | `sh start.sh --desktop` | | Windows PowerShell | `.\start.cmd --desktop` | | Windows 命令提示符 | `start.cmd --desktop` | [官网](https://soduwork.ai) | [在线体验](https://soduwork.ai) | [中文文档](docs/README.zh-CN.md) | [在线文档](https://dev.soduwork.ai/zh-CN/) | [Releases](https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork/releases) | [Discord](https://discord.gg/AXYNrAYHy) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/mdiri-ai/SoduWork)](https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork/releases) [![Platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20macOS%20%7C%20Linux-lightgrey.svg)](#快速开始) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/chat-Discord-5865F2.svg)](https://discord.gg/AXYNrAYHy)

**🔀 调度智能** **选对 Harness 和模型，让合适的 AI 做合适的事。** - 每个步骤各选 Harness，同一会话随时切换 - 常规步骤用经济型或本地模型，关键步骤用能力更强的模型 - 长任务交给自己的云端执行机继续 **🛡️ 治理闭环** **谁能用什么 AI、在哪台机器上做什么，由组织决定。** - 插件先审核再共享，可按部门或成员授权、随时撤回 - 部门角色、用量成本和审计日志都有记录 - 支持私有化部署 **✅ 结果交付** **先定标准再动手，需求方验收才算完成。** - 需求在开工前写明验收标准 - 独立的 AI 初审逐条对照检查 - 最终由人确认
## 快速开始 > SoduWork 处于公开测试阶段，欢迎试用并反馈；用于生产环境前请先充分评估。 准备好 Python 3.12+、Node.js 22.19+ 和 Git，两条命令跑起来： 在克隆后的目录里，macOS/Linux 运行 `sh start.sh --desktop`，Windows PowerShell 运行 `.\start.cmd --desktop`，命令提示符运行 `start.cmd --desktop`。 首次运行会自动安装依赖，在本机同时启动 Hub、管理端和桌面客户端。按提示为 `admin` 账号设置密码（12–128 位）。然后在管理端 **模型目录** 里接入模型服务，回到客户端新建对话，试一个小任务。Pi 已内置，开箱可用。 ### 已经添加 API Key，接下来怎么用？ 1. **再添加一个对话模型。** 在管理端「能力配置 → 模型目录」找到刚接入的服务，点「加模型」，填写服务商给出的准确模型 ID，选择「对话模型」并保存。API Key 是服务凭据，单独保存它不会创建可用模型。 2. **打开桌面客户端并登录同一个 Hub。** 源码启动使用 `--desktop`；浏览器管理端用于配置。核对登录页「连接」里的地址与刚才保存模型的管理端一致。 3. **点「新对话」，选择 Pi 和刚添加的模型。** Pi 使用 SoduWork 模型目录；Codex 使用自己的账号，还需要单独登录，不会自动使用这把 API Key。 4. **发一条小任务验证。** 例如：「把下面的模拟会议记录整理成待办表，列出负责人和截止时间；没有给出的信息写待确认：小王负责整理需求，周五完成；小李核对报价。」收到回复后检查表格内容。 5. **需要交办与验收时再创建需求。** 写清目标、材料和验收标准，打开需求的「安排执行」，选择 Agent 和模型，检查交付结果后再确认验收。普通对话不需要先创建项目、插件或自动化。 第一条消息建议使用 **OpenAI 兼容协议的对话模型 + Pi**。连接测试成功只表示探测通过，实际消息仍可能受到余额、模型权限或协议限制。底座列表为空时先检查「Agent 管理」的就绪状态及 Runner 连接；模型列表为空时核对模型是否已添加、启用，以及两端 Hub 地址是否一致。 完整字段说明、操作步骤和错误排查见[从零运行：发出第一条 AI 消息](docs/getting-started.md#发出第一条-ai-消息)。

## 架构概览 **这些难题，SoduWork 已经处理好：** | 难题 | SoduWork 怎么做 | | --- | --- | | 各端看到的事实不一致 | **Hub 是唯一状态来源**：需求、流程、审批和证据都以 Hub 为准，各端看到的是同一份事实 | | Agent 拿到不该有的权限 | **能力按授权开放**：组织策略、运行时可用性和用户选择共同决定一次会话能用什么，安装不等于授权 | | 被某一个 Harness 绑死 | **统一的 Harness 适配接口**：上层流程不依赖任何 Harness，会话中途切换，记录和目录都保留 | | 方法换个环境就用不了 | **方法与环境分开**：插件只定义做法，Harness、模型、执行机和密钥在绑定时决定；插件版本不可变、可迁移 | | 做过的事无从追溯 | **交互与执行分开**：客户端负责对话和审批，运行时和执行机负责干活，本机或远程都可以，每次运行都进入审计记录 |

执行机（Runner）内部

执行机通过 WebSocket 连接 Hub。每次派发都带编号，同一任务不会重复接收；每个 Harness 在独立子进程里运行；事件先在执行机落盘再发送，断线后自动补发。
使用边界 - **云端接力迁移的是上下文，不是进程**：工作文件、对话记录和目标会交给云端执行机，运行中的程序和浏览器登录状态不会迁移；云端执行机需要自行准备服务器。 - **插件不等于工作流**：插件可以只提供方法或工具；多阶段协作、人工确认和断点恢复才需要工作流。 - **执行机和技能不是通用安全沙箱**：实际隔离程度取决于 Harness 和部署环境，执行机只接入受信任的 Hub。
## 数据在哪里？ - **私有化部署时**，需求、插件和对话记录都存在你自己的 Hub 里，任务在你指定的目录中执行。 - **模型请求**由执行机直接发给你配置的模型服务；每次运行使用短期凭据，密钥不会以明文写进 Harness 的配置文件。 - **调用外部服务时**，提示词和相关文件会发给你配置的模型服务或连接器；使用自建模型时，推理也可以留在自己的环境中。 **遥测与更新。** 此公开源码没有单独向 MDiRi 上传分析或崩溃报告的功能。客户端默认连接 `https://service.soduwork.ai`，运行所需请求发送到登录页“连接”中选择的 Hub。用户可以更改地址，保存的选择会在重启和升级后保留。使用托管服务时，这些请求会发送给该服务的运营方；选择自己的 Hub 时，这些流量由自己的部署处理。 - 所选 Hub 接收设备和账号认证，以及你所用功能需要的数据。用量统计包含会话 ID 和标题、Agent／模型／供应商标识、Token 与费用计数以及时间。更新尝试会报告版本、进度、状态和错误。这些属于运行记录，并非可选的分析订阅。 - 安装版客户端会在启动时及之后每六小时向所选 Hub 检查更新，请求包含当前版本、平台、CPU 架构和更新通道，并使用设备会话认证。从源码启动的客户端跳过安装包更新检查。目前没有单独关闭 Hub 用量统计或安装版自动更新轮询的设置；如需避免向托管服务发送这些流量，请连接自己的 Hub。版本说明也从所选 Hub 读取。 - Hub 的请求和数据库性能统计保留在 Hub 进程内，不会自动上传到 MDiRi。依赖和可选 Agent 下载会访问配置的包仓库或镜像，模型与连接器会访问你配置的服务；这些服务各自适用其数据政策。 ## 常见问题
我一个人用，SoduWork 会不会太重？ 不会。只要你需要自己复查 AI 的产出、想复现上个月那次跑得很顺的流程，或者只是想让手上的 AI 工具用同一套标准，SoduWork 就用得上。个人使用不需要任何团队配置：一条命令用 SQLite 在本机跑起来，组织功能在你需要之前不会打扰你。插件和工作台都一样，想加人的时候再加。
这是不是又一个 Agent 平台或编排工具？ SoduWork 不替代 Agent Harness，而是把它们接进团队工作台，补上它们没有的那一层：从需求到验收的共享需求池、每个需求自带的验收标准、独立的 AI 初审、带分级授权的插件审核，以及完整的审计记录。工序、检查点和审批都由人设定。
项目在持续维护吗，还是只是个 Demo？ 在持续维护，目前处于公开测试阶段。每个版本都有发布说明，发布前会运行仓库检查和测试。接下来的计划见[路线图](#路线图)，想一起参与见[参与贡献](#参与贡献)。
为什么需要登录？数据存在哪里？ 账号是组织、权限、协作和审计的基础。私有化部署时，你登录的是自己的 Hub，数据也存在那里，见[数据在哪里？](#数据在哪里)
